faq.q: What is the weather like in Marbella in July 2028?
faq.a: July in Marbella brings hot, dry conditions: average highs of 30°C, lows around 22°C, sea temperature 24°C, and zero rain days historically. Expect 12+ hours of sunshine and light afternoon breezes.

faq.q: Is July a good month for a boat rental in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, July offers the best boating weather – calm seas, warm water, and clear skies. It's peak season, so book early. Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours with skipper included.

faq.q: What winds should I expect on a July boat charter?
faq.a: Typically light Levante winds from the east at 5–15 knots in the afternoon, calming mornings. The coast between Puerto Banús and Estepona remains sheltered, making for smooth cruising.

faq.q: Which boat is best for a group of 12 in July heat?
faq.a: The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) or Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) offer shaded flybridges, air-conditioned saloons, and plenty of deck space. Both depart from Puerto Banús.

faq.q: Can I swim from the boat in July?
faq.a: Absolutely – sea temperatures reach 24°C, ideal for swimming. Popular anchorages like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés have calm, clear water. All charters include safety equipment.

faq.q: Do I need to book a July charter in advance?
faq.a: Yes – July is peak season. We recommend booking 4–6 weeks ahead, especially for larger yachts like the Ferretti 94 (29m) or Mangusta 80. Contact us via WhatsApp for availability.

faq.q: What is included in a July boat rental?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety gear, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs.

faq.q: Are there any weather risks in July?
faq.a: Risks are minimal – thunderstorms are rare. Occasionally, strong Levante winds can cause choppy seas. Our skippers monitor forecasts and adjust itineraries to ensure safety and comfort.

data.body_html:
July in Marbella delivers the Mediterranean at its finest: 30°C air, 24°C sea, and zero rain days. For your Marbella boat rental weather July 2028 planning, this guide gives you the numbers, the best boats, and the local know-how to make your day on the water flawless. All charters depart from Puerto Banús with a skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks included.

July 2028 Weather Averages for Marbella

Based on 30-year climate data and 2028 projections:

  • Air temperature: 30°C high / 22°C low
  • Sea surface temperature: 24°C
  • Rain days: 0 (historical average)
  • Sunshine: 12+ hours per day
  • Wind: Light Levante 5–15 knots, mainly after 2 PM

These conditions are ideal for cruising, swimming, and anchoring off Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. Morning departures (9–10 AM) offer the calmest seas.

Best Boats for July Heat

With midday temperatures hitting 30°C, shaded decks and air-conditioned cabins are a bonus. Our fleet has options for every group size:

  • Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) – flybridge shade, A/C saloon
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – spacious sundeck, jet ski included on 4h+ charters (€4,719 minimum)
  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) – budget-friendly at €749/2h, great for smaller groups
  • Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) – ultimate luxury with full A/C

For a full list, see our Marbella boat rental fleet page.

Where to Go on a July Charter

Popular routes from Puerto Banús:

  • West to Estepona (8 NM) – calm waters, beach clubs, and the marina
  • East to Cabopino (6 NM) – quiet coves and the Artola dunes
  • Anchoring at Cala Cortés – crystal water, 24°C swimming
  • Sotogrande (20 NM) – exclusive port, worth a full-day trip

Your skipper will adapt to wind and swell for a smooth ride.

Pricing for July 2028

Peak-season rates are fixed – no surge pricing. Key options:

  • Tier A (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39): €749/2h → €2,299/8h (skipper + drinks + VAT included)
  • Mangusta 80 (white or grey): €4,719 minimum 4h (jet ski included free)
  • Other boats (e.g., Canados 86, Pershing 46): pricing on request via WhatsApp

All charters include skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, snacks, insurance, and IVA. No hidden fees.

What to Pack for a July Boat Day

  • Sunblock SPF 50+ (reapply every 2 hours)
  • Hat, sunglasses, light long-sleeve shirt
  • Swimwear and towel
  • Light jacket or windbreaker for afternoon breeze
  • Camera – the Golden Mile views are stunning

We provide chilled drinks and snacks, but you can bring your own food (no glass bottles).

Booking Tips for Peak Season

July is the busiest month. To secure your preferred yacht:

  • Book 4–6 weeks in advance
  • Weekdays (Mon–Thu) have more availability
  • 8-hour charters allow time for lunch at a beach club
  • Contact us via WhatsApp for instant confirmation on larger yachts

For more seasonal advice, read our Marbella boat rental weather July 2028 guide.
